title: January: Homeowners Plan Projects — Be Ready in 2027
meta: After the holidays, homeowners start planning remodels and repairs. Be findable and answer fast — or the next contractor gets the job. Here's how.
short: After the holidays people plan projects. Be findable and answer fast.

body.answer: After the holidays, homeowners start planning repairs and remodels. The contractors who win are the ones who are easy to find and answer fast.
body.html:
The decorations come down and the planning starts. Homeowners sit at the kitchen table thinking about the bathroom, the furnace that struggled all winter, the roof that's one more season from trouble. January is planning time.

You don't need to invent a seasonal story. You just need to be two things: easy to find when they search, and fast to answer when they reach out. Miss either and the job goes to whoever nailed both.

body.answer: Make sure your Google Business Profile and website show up and look legit when a homeowner searches your trade plus their town.
body.html:
When a homeowner finally searches 'furnace repair' plus their town, your Google Business Profile needs to be there, complete, and full of photos and reviews. If it's thin or unclaimed, you're invisible at the exact moment they're ready to act.

Walk the Google Business Profile checklist for contractors and make sure your site clearly says what you do and where. Reviews seal it — most homeowners read online reviews before choosing a contractor, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey).

body.h2: Answer fast or lose the lead
body.answer: When a planning homeowner reaches out, minutes matter. Responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect.
body.html:
A homeowner in planning mode is contacting a few shops at once. Whoever answers first usually wins the conversation. Responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd). That's not a small edge. That's the whole ballgame.

Build the habit and the tools now. Read speed to lead for contractors and get your response time down before the January rush.

body.h2: Catch the calls you can't take
body.answer: You'll be on jobs when the phone rings. Missed-call text-back keeps planning homeowners from calling the next contractor.
body.html:
Here's the catch. January planning calls come in while you're still finishing out the year's work. You can't always grab the phone. If that call hits voicemail, the homeowner moves down their list.

Set up missed-call text-back so every missed call gets an instant text: 'Sorry I missed you — what do you need?' That one text keeps the lead warm until you can call back. Want help wiring it up? Talk to Aaron.

faq.q: Why do homeowners plan projects in January?
faq.a: The holidays are over, budgets reset for the new year, and people have time to think about the repairs and remodels they put off. Be ready to be found.

faq.q: How fast do I really need to respond?
faq.a: Fast. Responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd).

faq.q: What if I can't answer the phone on a job?
faq.a: Missed-call text-back sends an automatic text so the homeowner knows you'll call back — before they dial the next contractor on their list.
